title: UX issue when mapping shortcuts (niche)
summary: Keyboard Manager can retain an EmptyAppName validation error after a valid app name is entered because that text change does not trigger the existing validation flow.

judgment.rationale: The supplied steps and video are reproducible, and source inspection identifies missing application-name TextChanged validation wiring in the Keyboard Manager editor.
evidence: The reporter says entering a valid application does not clear the app-specific validation error, while switching the right-side shortcut type does.
AppNameTextBox has a GotFocus handler but no TextChanged handler.
MainPage re-runs ValidateMapping when UnifiedMappingControl raises ValidationStateChanged.
ValidationHelper returns EmptyAppName when app-specific scope is enabled and the application name is blank.
Existing UI coverage does not assert that the validation error clears immediately after typing a valid application name.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the focused Keyboard Manager design available, but recheck for the contributor's promised pull request before starting duplicate implementation.

confidence.rationale: The reported behavior directly matches the missing TextChanged-to-validation wiring in the live source.

fix_assessment.rationale: A community contributor announced that they will raise a pull request, but no open or merged fix, assignment, linked pull request, or other concrete implementation covering this issue exists yet.

proposed_fixes.title: Revalidate app-specific mappings when the application name changes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: AppNameTextBox changes are not connected to UnifiedMappingControl.ValidationStateChanged, while EmptyAppName is checked by MainPage.ValidateMapping. The initial invalid state therefore remains stale after a valid application name is entered.
plan: Add an AppNameTextBox TextChanged handler in UnifiedMappingControl.xaml.
Raise the existing validation-state notification from the handler while preserving focus and keyboard-hook behavior.
Avoid unwanted validation during internal initialization or SetAppSpecific.
Extend KeyboardManagerEditorTests to prove the error clears and Save becomes enabled immediately after a valid application name is entered.
verification: Run the focused Keyboard Manager editor UI test covering app-specific validation.
Manually reproduce the reported sequence and verify the error disappears immediately after entering a valid application name.
Confirm the mapping can be saved without changing the right-side shortcut type.

confidence.rationale: The source event wiring and validation flow directly explain the reported stale state.

issue_context.summary: A Keyboard Manager app-specific shortcut dialog can retain the missing-application validation error after a valid application name is entered. Changing the action type clears the stale state.
known_information: The issue reports PowerToys 0.100.0 installed through auto-update on Windows 11.
The affected area is Keyboard Manager shortcut creation.
The reporter supplied numbered reproduction steps, a video, and a diagnostic ZIP.
The issue has no assignee and no linked fix.
A community contributor stated that they will raise a pull request, but no assignment, linked pull request, or concrete implementation exists yet.
The likely owning area is KeyboardManagerEditorUI and its UI tests.
inferences: The stale error is most likely caused by missing validation notification from AppNameTextBox.TextChanged rather than incorrect application-name validation.
The reset after switching shortcut type is consistent with another control raising ValidationStateChanged.
issue_context.analysis: ValidationHelper correctly rejects a blank app name, but AppNameTextBox does not notify the validation flow when its text changes. Other control changes do notify validation, explaining why an unrelated shortcut-type change clears the stale error. The latest discussion establishes intended community ownership, not a concrete fix, so the design remains valid but should be rechecked for duplicate work before implementation starts.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue, labels, attachments, and public comment.
Checked the public timeline and references for duplicate or covering work.
Inspected AppNameTextBox XAML, MainPage validation handling, ValidationHelper, and existing Keyboard Manager UI tests.
Reviewed the history introducing the WinUI 3 Keyboard Manager editor.

actions.label: Design fix for stale app-specific validation
actions.rationale: The investigation identifies a high-confidence localized fix path with no known ownership conflict.

reproduce.version: PowerToys 0.100.0 or the current build under test
steps: Open Keyboard Manager and create a new shortcut mapping.
Choose a multi-key trigger and a valid action shortcut.
Enable app-specific scope and observe the missing-application error.
Check whether the error clears and Save becomes enabled without changing another control.
reproduce.expected_result: Typing a valid application name immediately clears EmptyAppName and enables Save when the other inputs are valid.
reproduce.actual_result_reported: The error remains until the right-side shortcut type is changed.

author: Linus-Baumann
